title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 24
paragraphs: As I form my own judgment of this project, it seems to me that when Xerxes ordered the digging he was moved by a love of magnificence and by a wish to make a display of his power and leave a memorial behind. They could have dragged the ships across the isthmus with no great trouble, yet he had them dig a channel for the sea wide enough for two triremes to sail through side by side under oar. The same men to whom the digging had been assigned were also charged with throwing a bridge across the river Strymon, yoking its banks together.
